Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 3a) shows the azygos fissure as a distinct curvilinear line in the right upper lung field, but the characteristic teardrop-shaped opacity of the azygos vein at its caudal end is absent. This "empty azygos fissure" sign indicates that the azygos lobe has shifted or the vein has been displaced due to the pneumothorax and subsequent lung collapse/re-expansion dynamics, distinguishing it from the normal appearance where the vein is visible.
